# Block cookbook (risepath.lesson/v1)

Which block to use for which teaching job. Good examples are copied from the block gallery (`content/examples/blocks-gallery.lesson.json`,
rendered at `/dev/blocks?dev=1`); bad examples show the mistake and the lint rule it trips.
Every block also accepts `id` (required, unique in the lesson), `cite` (source ids), `narration` and `slide`.

## Pick a block by what the learner should do

| 学習者にさせたいこと / learner job | Block | Usual section role |
|---|---|---|
| 新しい考えを読む / read a new idea | [`markdown`](#markdown) | concept, example |
| たとえで直観をつかむ・つまずきを避ける / grasp by analogy, avoid a pitfall | [`callout`](#callout) | concept, pitfalls |
| 並列の項目を見渡す / scan parallel items | [`list`](#list) | concept, practice |
| 用語を覚える / learn terms | [`definitions`](#definitions) | concept |
| 比べる / compare | [`table`](#table) | concept, example |
| コードを読む・写す / read or type code | [`code`](#code) | example, practice |
| AI に依頼する / instruct an AI | [`prompt`](#prompt) | example, practice |
| 構造・流れを見る / see structure or flow | [`diagram`](#diagram) | concept |
| 画面を確かめる / check a screen | [`image`](#image) | example, practice |
| 予想する・思い出す・確かめる / predict, retrieve, check | [`quiz`](#quiz) | hook (predict), concept/example (inline), check (exam) |
| 間隔をあけて復習する / spaced review | [`flashcards`](#flashcards) | summary |
| 手順をたどる / follow a procedure | [`steps`](#steps) | example (worked), practice |
| できたか確かめる / confirm success | [`checklist`](#checklist) | practice |
| 要点を持ち帰る / take away the key points | [`summary`](#summary) | summary (required in the last section) |
| AI先生に聞く / ask the AI tutor | [`askTutor`](#asktutor) | concept, practice, reflection |

## Section roles, in reading order

| role | Typical blocks |
|---|---|
| `hook` | markdown (the problem, ≤ 3 sentences) + quiz mode "predict" |
| `concept` | markdown, callout analogy, definitions, diagram, table + quiz mode "inline" (one idea per section) |
| `example` | steps or code as a worked example with subgoal labels, then quiz "inline" |
| `practice` | markdown (task + success criteria), steps or prompt (hints in `hint`/`troubleshoot`, model answer in `expect`), checklist |
| `pitfalls` | callout pitfall (one real mistake: symptom → cause → fix); optional if the segments already cover it |
| `check` | quiz mode "exam" covering every objective, at least one apply question |
| `summary` | summary (3–5 points) + flashcards (4–8) |
| `reflection` | markdown (one question to think about) + askTutor; the reader adds a per-objective confidence check at the end |

## Blocks

### markdown

Prose paragraph(s). Keep each paragraph within 160 JP characters / 80 EN words.

Fields: `md`; `style`? (`normal` | `lead` | `quote`).

**Use**
- Explanation prose. One idea per block; at most 160 JP characters per paragraph and 60 per sentence (80 EN words).
- `style: "lead"` for the first paragraph of a lesson or section; `"quote"` for a quoted statement.
- Inline markdown only: **bold** (at most 1–2 per paragraph), `code`, [descriptive link](https://…), [[glossary term]].

**Avoid**
- Lists written as paragraphs, and "**Label**: text" lines (use `definitions`).
- Raw HTML, headings inside md (sections have titles), *italics* in Japanese (use 「」).

**Lint**: `paragraph-length` (A paragraph is at most 160 JP characters or 80 EN/FR words.); `sentence-length` (A JP sentence is at most 60 characters.); `banned-phrase` (No pressuring phrases (「簡単です」「誰でも」, "simply", "obviously").)

**Good** — gallery block `prose-md` (section `prose`):

```json
{
  "id": "prose-md",
  "type": "markdown",
  "md": {
    "jp": "本文は `markdown` ブロックで書きます。**太字**、`インラインコード`、[外部リンク](https://developer.mozilla.org/ja/docs/Web/HTML)、用語へのリンク [[lint]] が使えます。\n\n1つの段落は160字以内、1文は60字以内を目安にします。段落にカーソルを合わせると、右側に ✦ が出ます。",
    "en": "Body text goes in a `markdown` block. It supports **bold**, `inline code`, [external links](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML) and glossary links such as [[lint]].\n\nKeep a paragraph under 80 words. Hover a paragraph to reveal the ✦ ask button on its right."
  }
}
```

**Bad** — trips `banned-phrase`:

```json
{
  "id": "intro",
  "type": "markdown",
  "md": "プログラミングは簡単です。誰でもすぐに書けるようになります。変数や関数、条件分岐、繰り返し、配列、オブジェクト、クラス、非同期処理など、覚えることはたくさんありますが、ひとつずつ覚えれば大丈夫です。まずは全部をざっと眺めて、雰囲気をつかむところから始めましょう。分からなくても気にせず、どんどん先へ進んでください。"
}
```

Why: Pressure phrases (簡単です, 誰でも), eight new terms at once, and a paragraph over 160 characters (paragraph-length). Split by idea and define each term where it is first needed.

### callout

Highlighted note. At most 2 per section; an analogy goes before the formal definition.

Fields: `variant` (`tip` | `warning` | `info` | `analogy` | `pitfall` | `note` | `success`); `title`?; `md`.

**Use**
- `analogy` before the formal definition (never quiz the analogy itself). In a `level: "beginner"` lesson, an everyday analogy before the definition of each new term, saying what maps to what; one may cover a segment's related terms, and it may sit in the text instead.
- `pitfall` for one real, common error per segment, with how to notice and fix it.
- `warning` for data loss, security or cost; `tip`, `info`, `note`, `success` (expected result after a task).
- At most 2 callouts per section, at most 3 sentences each.

**Avoid**
- Stacking callouts, or putting the main explanation in one.
- Vague warnings ("注意してください") that do not say what to do.

**Lint**: `callout-count` (At most 2 callouts per section.)

**Good** — gallery block `prose-analogy` (section `prose`):

```json
{
  "id": "prose-analogy",
  "type": "callout",
  "variant": "analogy",
  "title": {"jp":"たとえるなら","en":"Think of it like this"},
  "md": {
    "jp": "ブロックはレゴの部品のようなものです。形が決まっているので、だれが組み立てても同じように表示されます。",
    "en": "Blocks are like LEGO bricks. Each has a fixed shape, so a lesson looks the same whoever builds it."
  }
}
```

**Bad** — a reviewer catches this:

```json
{"id":"warn","type":"callout","variant":"warning","md":"エラーが出ることがあるので注意してください。"}
```

Why: Says neither which error, nor why, nor what to do. A pitfall callout names the mistake, the symptom and the fix.

### list

Bulleted, numbered or check list (7 items max). Use definitions for "label: description" items.

Fields: `style`? (`bullet` | `number` | `check`); `items`.

**Use**
- 3–7 parallel, short items. `style: "number"` for an order without expected results (otherwise use `steps`), `"check"` for criteria.

**Avoid**
- More than 7 items (split or group).
- Items shaped "**Label**: description" (use `definitions`).

**Lint**: `list-length` (A list has at most 7 items.); `list-definitions` ("**Label**: description" lists are definitions blocks.)

**Good** — gallery block `prose-list` (section `prose`):

```json
{
  "id": "prose-list",
  "type": "list",
  "style": "bullet",
  "items": [
    {"jp":"段落は `markdown`","en":"Paragraphs: `markdown`"},
    {"jp":"補足や注意は `callout`","en":"Side notes and warnings: `callout`"},
    {"jp":"並んだ項目は `list`","en":"Items in a row: `list`"}
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `list-definitions`:

```json
{"id":"parts","type":"list","items":["**フロントエンド**: 画面の部分","**バックエンド**: サーバーの部分","**データベース**: データの保存場所"]}
```

Why: Every item is a term plus its meaning; a definitions block renders and reads better.

### definitions

Term / description pairs, rendered as a definition list.

Fields: `items`.

Each `items` item: `term`; `md`.

**Use**
- The first definition of new terms, at most 3 new terms per segment. Mirror each term in `glossary` and mark later uses as [[term]].
- Katakana terms carry the English on first use: 参照（reference）.

**Avoid**
- A glossary dump of terms the lesson never uses.
- Defining a term after it has already been used.

**Good** — gallery block `prose-defs` (section `prose`):

```json
{
  "id": "prose-defs",
  "type": "definitions",
  "items": [
    {
      "term": {"jp":"レッスン","en":"Lesson"},
      "md": {"jp":"1回で学び終える単位。15〜20分が目安。","en":"One sitting of learning, about 15–20 minutes."}
    },
    {
      "term": {"jp":"セクション","en":"Section"},
      "md": {"jp":"見出しの付いたブロックのまとまり。目次に1行ずつ並ぶ。","en":"A titled group of blocks; one row in the contents."}
    },
    {
      "term": {"jp":"ブロック","en":"Block"},
      "md": {"jp":"セクションの中に並ぶ部品。`type` で種類が決まる。","en":"A piece inside a section; its `type` decides what it is."}
    }
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — a reviewer catches this:

```json
{"id":"terms","type":"definitions","items":[{"term":"API","md":"色々なものをつなぐもの。"}]}
```

Why: "色々なものをつなぐもの" explains nothing. A definition says what it is, what it does, and an example the learner knows.

### table

Data table (6 columns max). Every row has one cell per column.

Fields: `caption`?; `columns`; `rows`.

**Use**
- Compare 2–4 things across the same attributes. At most 6 columns; a caption that states what the comparison shows.

**Avoid**
- Tables for sequences (use `steps`) or for layout.
- Long prose inside cells.

**Lint**: `table-columns` (A table has at most 6 columns.)

**Good** — gallery block `visuals-table` (section `visuals`):

```json
{
  "id": "visuals-table",
  "type": "table",
  "caption": {"jp":"見せ方のブロックと決まりごと","en":"Visual blocks and their rules"},
  "columns": [{"jp":"ブロック","en":"Block"},{"jp":"使う場面","en":"Use it for"},{"jp":"決まりごと","en":"Rules"}],
  "rows": [
    [
      {"jp":"`table`","en":"`table`"},
      {"jp":"項目を比べる","en":"Comparing items"},
      {"jp":"6列まで、キャプションを付ける","en":"Up to 6 columns, with a caption"}
    ],
    [
      {"jp":"`diagram`","en":"`diagram`"},
      {"jp":"流れや関係を見せる","en":"Showing a flow or a relation"},
      {"jp":"ノード12個まで、キャプションと alt","en":"Up to 12 nodes, caption and alt"}
    ],
    [
      {"jp":"`image`","en":"`image`"},
      {"jp":"画面や実物を見せる","en":"Showing a real screen or object"},
      {"jp":"alt 必須、飾りの画像は使わない","en":"Alt required, no decorative images"}
    ]
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `table-columns`:

```json
{
  "id": "cmp",
  "type": "table",
  "columns": ["名前","速さ","価格","難しさ","人気","対応OS","日本語","サポート"],
  "rows": [["A","速い","無料","低","高","全部","あり","メール"]]
}
```

Why: 8 columns do not fit a phone. Keep the 3–4 attributes that matter for the objective.

### code

Source code (25 lines max inline). Instructions to an AI go in a prompt block, not here.

Fields: `lang` — Language id for highlighting, e.g. ts, bash, json, python; `code`; `filename`? — Shown in the code header. Recommended; `highlight`? — 1-based line numbers to emphasize.

**Use**
- Code the learner reads or runs: always `lang` and `filename`, at most 25 lines, runnable as written, `highlight` the lines the text talks about.
- Ask for a prediction before showing output; state the expected output after it, not in comments.

**Avoid**
- Instructions to an AI (use `prompt`).
- Pseudo-code that looks runnable but is not.

**Lint**: `code-filename` (Code blocks have a filename.); `code-length` (Inline code is at most 25 lines.); `code-should-be-prompt` (Instructions to an AI (lang markdown/text, or a "prompt" filename) use a prompt block.)

**Good** — gallery block `code-ts` (section `code`):

```json
{
  "id": "code-ts",
  "type": "code",
  "lang": "ts",
  "filename": "firstTryRate.ts",
  "code": "type Answer = { attempts: number; correct: boolean };\n\nexport function firstTryRate(answers: Answer[]): number {\n  const answered = answers.filter((a) => a.attempts > 0);\n  if (answered.length === 0) return 0;\n  const firstTry = answered.filter((a) => a.correct && a.attempts === 1);\n  return Math.round((firstTry.length / answered.length) * 100);\n}\n\nfirstTryRate([\n  { attempts: 1, correct: true },\n  { attempts: 2, correct: true },\n]); // → 50",
  "highlight": [6,7]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `code-should-be-prompt`:

```json
{"id":"ask-ai","type":"code","lang":"text","filename":"prompt.txt","code":"このファイルを読んで、改善点を教えてください。"}
```

Why: An instruction to an AI belongs in a prompt block, which adds copy, variables and the expected answer.

### prompt

A prompt the learner can copy into an AI tool. Every example instruction to an AI uses this block.

Fields: `title`?; `prompt` — The instruction to give an AI. {{name}} marks an editable variable; `target`? (`any` | `claude` | `claude-code` | `chatgpt` | `gemini`); `vars`?; `expect`? — What a good AI answer looks like (shown collapsed); `note`?.

Each `vars` item: `name` — Variable name as written inside {{ }} in the prompt; `hint`?.

**Use**
- Every example instruction to an AI tool. `target` (claude-code, chatgpt, …), `{{variables}}` with `vars[].hint`, and `expect`: what a good answer looks like (shown collapsed — doubles as the model answer).
- In a multi-locale lesson the variable names differ per locale; list each name in `vars` (see the gallery).

**Avoid**
- Vague asks ("いい感じに作って").
- Secrets, keys or personal data in the prompt.

**Good** — gallery block `practice-prompt-chat` (section `practice`):

```json
{
  "id": "practice-prompt-chat",
  "type": "prompt",
  "target": "chatgpt",
  "title": {"jp":"チャットAIへの質問","en":"A question for a chat AI"},
  "prompt": {
    "jp": "中学生にも分かるように、{{用語}} を身近なたとえで説明してください。",
    "en": "Explain {{term}} with an everyday analogy a 14-year-old would follow."
  },
  "vars": [{"name":"用語","hint":{"jp":"例：API","en":"e.g. API"}},{"name":"term","hint":{"jp":"例：API","en":"e.g. API"}}]
}
```

**Bad** — a reviewer catches this:

```json
{"id":"make-app","type":"prompt","prompt":"いい感じのアプリを作って。"}
```

Why: No goal, constraint or expected result, so the learner cannot tell a good answer. Add context, `{{variables}}` and `expect`.

### diagram

Mermaid diagram (12 nodes max) with caption and alt text. Mind maps use mermaid "mindmap" syntax.

Fields: `engine` (`mermaid`); `code` — Mermaid source (flowchart, sequence, er, mindmap, …). May be localized per locale; `caption`?; `alt` — Short text alternative for screen readers; `description`? — Longer prose explanation shown under the figure.

**Use**
- Only for structure, process, state change or comparison. Mermaid flowchart, sequence, er or mindmap; at most 12 nodes.
- Labels in the lesson language (localize `code` per locale when labels differ), the same terms as the text.
- `caption` states the takeaway; `alt` is one sentence; `description` holds the long explanation.
- Prefer `flowchart TD` for chains longer than 4 nodes: wide LR diagrams scroll sideways on phones.

**Avoid**
- Decorative diagrams that repeat the text.
- English-only labels in a Japanese lesson.
- Mermaid init directives or styling (the reader themes diagrams).

**Lint**: `diagram-caption` (Diagrams have a caption.)

**Good** — gallery block `visuals-flow` (section `visuals`):

```json
{
  "id": "visuals-flow",
  "type": "diagram",
  "engine": "mermaid",
  "code": {
    "jp": "flowchart LR\n  A[下書きを書く] --> B[validate で検証]\n  B --> C[lint で読みやすさを確認]\n  C --> D[プレビューで見た目を確認]\n  D --> E((公開))",
    "en": "flowchart LR\n  A[Write a draft] --> B[Validate the schema]\n  B --> C[Lint for readability]\n  C --> D[Preview the page]\n  D --> E((Publish))"
  },
  "caption": {"jp":"教材を公開するまでの流れ","en":"From draft to published lesson"},
  "alt": {
    "jp": "下書き、検証、lint、プレビュー、公開の5段階が左から右へ矢印でつながっている図",
    "en": "Five steps joined by arrows from left to right: draft, validate, lint, preview, publish"
  },
  "description": {
    "jp": "最初に下書きを書き、`validate` でスキーマを検証します。次に `lint` で読みやすさのルールを確かめ、プレビューで見た目を確認してから公開します。",
    "en": "Write a draft, then `validate` the schema. Next, `lint` checks the readability rules, and a preview shows the page before you publish."
  }
}
```

**Bad** — trips `diagram-caption`:

```json
{
  "id": "flow",
  "type": "diagram",
  "engine": "mermaid",
  "code": "graph LR\n  User --> Frontend --> API --> Backend --> DB",
  "alt": "Web app flow"
}
```

Why: No caption, English labels in a JP lesson, and a long LR chain that overflows a phone.

### image

A teaching image (screenshot, comparison). Alt text is required.

Fields: `src`; `alt`; `caption`?; `layout`? (`inline` | `wide`); `decorative`? — Decorative images belong on the course cover only.

**Use**
- Teaching images only: screenshots, before/after comparisons. `alt` says what matters in the picture; `caption` ties it to the text.

**Avoid**
- Stock photos or decoration (they lower recall).
- Text baked into images.
- Invented URLs: use a file that exists under public/, or ask the owner for one.

**Lint**: `image-decorative` (No decorative or stock-photo images inside a lesson.)

**Good** — gallery block `visuals-image` (section `visuals`):

```json
{
  "id": "visuals-image",
  "type": "image",
  "src": "/teacher-bot/media/editors_3dview_navigate_introduction_gizmo.png",
  "alt": {
    "jp": "Blender の3Dビュー右上にあるナビゲーションギズモ。X・Y・Z 軸の丸いボタンの下に、ズーム・移動・カメラ・グリッドのアイコンが縦に並んでいる。",
    "en": "Blender's navigation gizmo in the top-right of the 3D view: round X, Y and Z axis buttons above zoom, pan, camera and grid icons."
  },
  "caption": {
    "jp": "画像ブロックの例：Blender のナビゲーションギズモ（スクリーンショット）",
    "en": "Image block example: Blender's navigation gizmo (screenshot)"
  }
}
```

**Bad** — trips `image-decorative`:

```json
{"id":"hero","type":"image","src":"https://images.unsplash.com/photo-123","alt":"笑顔でパソコンを使う人"}
```

Why: A stock photo teaches nothing and distracts. Show the actual screen the learner will see, or nothing.

### quiz

Retrieval practice. Place an inline quiz at least every 2 sections.

Fields: `mode` (`inline` | `exam` | `predict`) — inline = a check while reading (確認しよう); exam = end-of-lesson test; predict = an ungraded prediction in the hook (the pick is not scored; the explanation is revealed after answering); `title`?; `questions`.

Each `questions` item: `id`; `kind`? (`single` | `multi` | `truefalse`) — Defaults to single; `prompt`; `options`; `answer` — Ids of the correct options; `explanation`; `hint`?; `objectiveId`? — The lesson objective this question assesses. Required when the lesson has objectives; `bloom`?.

Each `options` item: `id`; `md`; `feedback`? — Shown when this option is picked. Required for wrong options: name and correct the misconception in 2 sentences.

**Use**
- `predict` in the hook: ungraded; the explanation reveals the answer.
- `inline` at least once per 2 content sections, 1–2 questions, right after the idea.
- `exam` in the check section: covers every objective, at least one apply-level question.
- Every question: `objectiveId`, 3–4 options, `feedback` on every wrong option (≤ 2 sentences naming the misconception), `explanation`, `bloom`.

**Avoid**
- Quizzing the analogy, the anecdote or trivia.
- "All of the above"; answers findable by matching words in the previous sentence.

**Lint**: `objective-unassessed` (Every objective is assessed by at least one quiz question.); `inline-quiz-density` (At least one inline quiz per 2 content sections, and never 3 content sections in a row without one.); `quiz-feedback` (Every wrong option has feedback that corrects the misconception.); `feedback-length` (Option feedback is at most 2 sentences.)

**Good** — gallery block `prose-check` (section `prose`):

```json
{
  "id": "prose-check",
  "type": "quiz",
  "mode": "inline",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "prose-q1",
      "prompt": {"jp":"日本語の1つの段落の長さは、何字以内が目安でしょう？","en":"What is the length limit for one Japanese paragraph?"},
      "options": [
        {
          "id": "a",
          "md": {"jp":"80字","en":"80 characters"},
          "feedback": {"jp":"80字だと短すぎて、説明が細切れになりがちです。","en":"80 is too short; explanations get chopped into pieces."}
        },
        {"id":"b","md":{"jp":"160字","en":"160 characters"}},
        {
          "id": "c",
          "md": {"jp":"400字","en":"400 characters"},
          "feedback": {
            "jp": "400字は画面で5〜6行になり、読み飛ばされやすくなります。",
            "en": "400 characters fill five or six lines, and readers start to skim."
          }
        }
      ],
      "answer": ["b"],
      "explanation": {
        "jp": "160字はおよそ3〜4行です。それより長くなったら、段落を分けるか、リストや表に置き換えます。",
        "en": "160 characters is about three or four lines. Anything longer is split, or turned into a list or a table."
      },
      "hint": {"jp":"スマートフォンの画面で、3〜4行に収まる長さを考えてみましょう。","en":"Think of what fits in three or four lines on a phone."},
      "objectiveId": "o1",
      "bloom": "remember"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `quiz-feedback`:

```json
{
  "id": "q1",
  "type": "quiz",
  "mode": "inline",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1a",
      "prompt": "API は何の略？",
      "options": [{"id":"a","md":"Application Programming Interface"},{"id":"b","md":"Apple Pie Inc."}],
      "answer": ["a"],
      "explanation": "API は Application Programming Interface の略です。",
      "objectiveId": "o1"
    }
  ]
}
```

Why: Recall of an acronym, a joke distractor and no feedback on the wrong option. Ask the learner to apply the idea in a new situation, with one distractor per real misconception.

### flashcards

Review cards (4–8 per lesson) that feed the review queue.

Fields: `cards`.

Each `cards` item: `id`; `front`; `back`.

**Use**
- 4–8 cards per lesson, one fact or cue each; the front is a question or cue, the back a short answer.

**Avoid**
- Copying paragraphs onto cards.
- More than 8 cards.

**Lint**: `flashcards-count` (A lesson has 4–8 flashcards.)

**Good** — gallery block `wrapup-cards` (section `wrapup`):

```json
{
  "id": "wrapup-cards",
  "type": "flashcards",
  "cards": [
    {
      "id": "card-1",
      "front": {"jp":"確認問題で2回まちがえると？","en":"What happens after two wrong answers?"},
      "back": {
        "jp": "正解と解説が表示される。ヒントはその前に見られる。",
        "en": "The answer and explanation appear. Hints are available before that."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "card-2",
      "front": {"jp":"[✦説明] が AI先生に送るものは？","en":"What does ✦ Explain send to the tutor?"},
      "back": {"jp":"コード全体と、強調された行の番号。","en":"The whole code and the highlighted line numbers."}
    },
    {
      "id": "card-3",
      "front": {"jp":"図に必ず付けるものは？","en":"What must every figure have?"},
      "back": {"jp":"キャプションと代替テキスト（alt）。","en":"A caption and alt text."}
    },
    {
      "id": "card-4",
      "front": {"jp":"AIへの指示文の例に使うブロックは？","en":"Which block holds an example AI instruction?"},
      "back": {"jp":"`prompt` ブロック。","en":"The `prompt` block."}
    },
    {
      "id": "card-5",
      "front": {"jp":"1つの段落の目安は？","en":"How long can a paragraph be?"},
      "back": {"jp":"日本語で160字以内、英語で80語以内。","en":"Up to 160 Japanese characters or 80 English words."}
    }
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `flashcards-count`:

```json
{
  "id": "cards",
  "type": "flashcards",
  "cards": [
    {
      "id": "c1",
      "front": "API",
      "back": "Application Programming Interface。ソフトウェア同士をつなぐ窓口で、決まった形式でリクエストを送るとレスポンスが返ってきます。REST や GraphQL などの種類があります。"
    }
  ]
}
```

Why: One card, and its back is a paragraph. Use 4–8 cards with one short answer each.

### steps

A procedure (8 steps max), each with an expected result.

Fields: `items`.

Each `items` item: `id`; `title`; `md`?; `keys`? — Keyboard keys shown as <kbd> chips; `expect`? — Expected result of the step; `hint`?; `troubleshoot`?.

**Use**
- Procedures of at most 8 steps. Each step: a subgoal title, `expect` (what the learner sees), `keys` for shortcuts, `hint`, `troubleshoot`.
- Worked example: the same subgoal titles reused in the text; a faded version later leaves 1–2 steps for the learner.
- `cite` the sources the commands, menus and expected results come from. Name a menu, button, screen or shortcut only as the official docs of the pinned version show it; when you cannot check it, describe the goal instead of the clicks.
- Steps that only ask the learner to write or decide have nothing to cite: keep the `steps-cite` warning and give the reason in the report.

**Avoid**
- Steps without an expected result.
- Ten-step marathons (split into two blocks).
- Menus, buttons and shortcuts written from memory.
- A cite to a source that does not say it, just to quiet the lint.

**Lint**: `steps-length` (A steps block has at most 8 steps.); `steps-expect` (Every step states its expected result.); `steps-cite` (A steps block cites the sources that back its commands, menus and expected results.)

**Good** — gallery block `practice-steps` (section `practice`):

```json
{
  "id": "practice-steps",
  "type": "steps",
  "cite": ["vscode-terminal","vscode-ui","rp-readme","rp-validate","node-errors","rp-dev-blocks","chrome-shortcuts"],
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "step-1",
      "title": {"jp":"ターミナルを開く","en":"Open a terminal"},
      "md": {
        "jp": "VS Code では、メニューの「ターミナル → 新しいターミナル」からも開けます。",
        "en": "In VS Code you can also use Terminal → New Terminal."
      },
      "keys": ["Ctrl+`"],
      "expect": {"jp":"画面の下にターミナルが表示される。","en":"A terminal opens at the bottom of the window."}
    },
    {
      "id": "step-2",
      "title": {"jp":"検証コマンドを実行する","en":"Run the validator"},
      "md": {"jp":"`npm run lessons:validate` と入力して実行します。","en":"Type `npm run lessons:validate` and run it."},
      "keys": ["Enter"],
      "expect": {"jp":"最後の行に `no errors` と表示される。","en":"The last line says `no errors`."},
      "hint": {"jp":"プロジェクトのフォルダーで実行しているか確かめましょう。","en":"Check that you are in the project folder."},
      "troubleshoot": {
        "jp": "`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` と出たら、先に `npm install` を実行します。",
        "en": "If you see `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, run `npm install` first."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "step-3",
      "title": {"jp":"プレビューで確認する","en":"Check the preview"},
      "md": {
        "jp": "ブラウザで `/dev/blocks?dev=1` を開き、強制再読み込みします。",
        "en": "Open `/dev/blocks?dev=1` in the browser and force a reload."
      },
      "keys": ["Ctrl+Shift+R"],
      "expect": {"jp":"すべてのブロックが表示され、赤い警告が出ていない。","en":"Every block shows up and no red warning appears."}
    }
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `steps-expect`:

```json
{"id":"setup","type":"steps","items":[{"id":"s1","title":"ターミナルを開く"},{"id":"s2","title":"npm install を実行する"}]}
```

Why: The learner cannot tell whether a step worked, and nothing says where the steps come from (`steps-cite`). Add `expect` to every step and `cite` the docs they follow.

### checklist

Items the learner ticks off; state is saved.

Fields: `title`?; `items`.

Each `items` item: `id`; `label`; `md`?.

**Use**
- Success criteria of a practice task, or a setup check. At most 7 items; ticks are saved per learner.

**Avoid**
- Items that are instructions (use `steps`).

**Good** — gallery block `practice-checklist` (section `practice`):

```json
{
  "id": "practice-checklist",
  "type": "checklist",
  "title": {"jp":"公開前のチェックリスト","en":"Before you publish"},
  "items": [
    {"id":"publish-1","label":{"jp":"学習目標が2〜4個ある","en":"There are 2–4 objectives"}},
    {
      "id": "publish-2",
      "label": {"jp":"2セクションに1つ以上、確認問題がある","en":"Every two sections have at least one check"},
      "md": {"jp":"誤答の選択肢には、それぞれ解説を付けます。","en":"Each wrong option has its own feedback."}
    },
    {"id":"publish-3","label":{"jp":"図にキャプションと alt がある","en":"Figures have a caption and alt text"}},
    {"id":"publish-4","label":{"jp":"lint --strict の警告が0件","en":"lint --strict reports nothing"}}
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — a reviewer catches this:

```json
{"id":"done","type":"checklist","items":[{"id":"c1","label":"頑張った"}]}
```

Why: Not checkable. Each item names an observable result ("ブラウザに一覧が表示される").

### summary

Key takeaways (3–5 points). Required in the last section.

Fields: `title`?; `points`.

**Use**
- 3–5 points, each an outcome tied to an objective. Place it after the recap questions.

**Avoid**
- Repeating headings; new information.

**Lint**: `summary-missing` (The last section contains a summary block.); `summary-points` (A summary has 3–5 points.)

**Good** — gallery block `wrapup-summary` (section `wrapup`):

```json
{
  "id": "wrapup-summary",
  "type": "summary",
  "points": [
    {
      "jp": "文章は `markdown`、補足は `callout`、用語の対応は `definitions` で書く。",
      "en": "Prose in `markdown`, side notes in `callout`, term pairs in `definitions`."
    },
    {"jp":"図と表には、キャプションと代替テキストを必ず付ける。","en":"Figures and tables always get a caption and alt text."},
    {
      "jp": "AIへの指示は `prompt`、作業の手順は `steps` で見せる。",
      "en": "AI instructions go in `prompt`, procedures in `steps`."
    },
    {
      "jp": "確認問題は2セクションに1つ以上置き、誤答には解説を付ける。",
      "en": "Put a check in every two sections, with feedback on each wrong option."
    }
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — trips `summary-points`:

```json
{"id":"sum","type":"summary","points":["API について学びました。","フロントエンドについて学びました。"]}
```

Why: Two points that list topics, not takeaways. Write 3–5 statements the learner can now use.

### askTutor

Suggested questions that open the AI tutor.

Fields: `suggestions`.

**Use**
- 2–3 specific questions a learner is likely to have at this point; they open the AI tutor grounded in the lesson.

**Avoid**
- Generic suggestions ("質問はありますか？").

**Good** — gallery block `code-ask` (section `code`):

```json
{
  "id": "code-ask",
  "type": "askTutor",
  "suggestions": [
    {"jp":"強調された2行は何をしている？","en":"What do the two highlighted lines do?"},
    {"jp":"attempts === 1 の意味を教えて","en":"What does attempts === 1 mean?"},
    {"jp":"Python 版との違いは？","en":"How does the Python example differ?"}
  ]
}
```

**Bad** — a reviewer catches this:

```json
{"id":"ask","type":"askTutor","suggestions":["何でも聞いてください"]}
```

Why: Gives the learner nothing to start from. Suggest the questions a confused learner would actually ask here.
